source.title: Tula: Optimizing Time, Cost, and Generalization in Distributed Large-Batch Training

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether large-batch training degrades held-out performance and whether adaptive gradient scaling can mitigate that gap, using distributed convolutional training and test accuracy.
record.gate_note: Reports its own test-accuracy results for batch-size conditions and compares AGS with large-batch baselines. Cited prior findings about large-batch generalization are not treated as this study's results. Other reported results on runtime, cost, and prediction error do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own batch-size sweeps and held-out accuracy curves under common epoch schedules, directly testing V5, and evaluates gradient scaling as an additional recipe adaptation. It is not an original source for V5. Total epoch budgets for Table I are not explicitly specified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: larger batches degrade held-out accuracy, while AGS mitigates degradation, with a reported average improvement of 8.8% over vanilla training at the same effective batch size. Complete recovery to small-batch accuracy is not established.
record.recipe_differences: Distributed convolutional vision training on up to 16 nodes; tests batch-size effects and AGS, a per-parameter adaptive gradient scaling method, rather than the cited studies' large-batch interventions and fixed-epoch comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with model, dataset, global batch size, and AGS scaling choices; the text reports AlexNet's higher scaling factors can degrade performance, ResNet50 accuracy degrades when δ rises from 0.5 to 0.8, and VGG11 benefits from δ = 0.2. AGS update frequency and reference batch size are stated limitations, not evaluated outcome conditions here.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient norms, gradient variability and Hessian eigenvalues change during training and help identify sensitive phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First-order gradient statistics can track sensitive optimization phases.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Cluster, Cloud and Internet Computing
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for test accuracy. Only four convolutional vision models are evaluated. The relevant large-batch results are reported through a mix of prose, figures, and a flattened table; some Table I batch-to-value assignments are difficult to recover with confidence.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported test-accuracy results omitted. Rows R1–R4 use the prose trends and separately reported large-batch table values; non-claim performance-model time/cost and prediction-error results are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under the specified tuning regimes; AGS and LARS comparisons do not supply this experiment.

Language models; longer-training interventions; normalization or regularization interventions; explicit matched small-batch recovery under a documented equal total epoch budget. LR scaling and warmup are evaluated, so they should not be listed as wholly untested.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Batch-specific held-out results for LRS, LARS and PoLo are omitted despite directly bearing on recipe-dependent mitigation. For example, VGG11 LRS reaches 7.50, 5.00 and 5.00%, versus LBT 83.30, 75.92 and 70.24%; ResNet50 LARS reaches 83.26, 85.02 and 86.77%, versus LBT 79.67, 75.55 and 64.72%. All methods are reported with five warmup epochs. These results support V5's conditional recipe framing, rather than challenging it.

record.verdict_notes: Use the supplied text only. The AGS accuracy comparisons bear directly on V5's adaptation clause, so retain them despite their method-comparison format. Do not label mitigation as limits_scope merely because recovery is incomplete: V5 already allows partial mitigation. Static-scaling sensitivity results are already declared in the record's method_sensitivity field; omitted figure-only curves are acknowledged in its coverage note.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization in the same recipes, and held-out chance accuracy for random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD under the stated tuning conditions.

Language models; comparison across workloads to identify a workload-dependent batch threshold; within the same epoch budget, compensation by longer training, LR scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization changes, and small-batch-matching results.
Dropout additions and removals, training-set-size regimes, and dropout under/overfitting.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and test-accuracy comparison with random removals.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Train across global batch sizes and report top-5 test accuracy
rows.value: Test accuracy deteriorates as global batches grow; exact values are reported in Table I for LBT: 79.67, 75.55, 64.72 for batch sizes 1024, 2048, 4096, respectively.
rows.note: The table supplies LBT values for the listed large batches. The text states that accuracy declines as training batch size increases.
rows.check: Separate Figure 2's batch sweep from Table I's method comparison. Table I supplies only batches 1024, 2048 and 4096, with top-5 accuracies 79.67, 75.55 and 64.72%; smaller-batch numerical baselines are not transcribed.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Train across global batch sizes and report top-1 test accuracy
rows.value: Test accuracy deteriorates as global batches grow; Table I reports LBT values of 83.30, 75.92, 70.24 for batch sizes 1024, 2048, 4096, respectively.
rows.note: The text says VGG11 shows a similar declining trend; Table I gives the LBT accuracy values.
rows.check: Separate Figure 2's batch sweep from Table I. The table supplies only batches 1024, 2048 and 4096, with top-1 accuracies 83.30, 75.92 and 70.24%; smaller-batch numerical baselines are not transcribed.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Train across global batch sizes and report top-1 test accuracy
rows.value: The text reports accuracy dropped from 82% to 37% as batch size increased from 128 to 2048; Table I reports LBT values of 80.62, 72.80, 62.60 for batch sizes 256, 512, 1024.
rows.note: The stated 82% to 37% endpoints are reported in §II-B; Table I provides additional LBT values for other listed batch sizes.
rows.check: The prose gives 82% at batch 128 and 37% at 2048, but Figure 2's extracted legend lists 32, 128, 512, 1024, 1536 and 2048. Batch 256 belongs to Table I, not that legend. Preserve the prose endpoints and table results as separate conditions.

rows.subject: MobileNetv3
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Train across global batch sizes and report top-1 test accuracy
rows.value: The text reports accuracy degraded from 80% to 20% as batch size increased from 256 to 8192; Table I reports LBT values of 76.80, 71.15, 66.48 for batch sizes 1024, 2048, 4096.
rows.note: The stated endpoints are from §II-B; Table I provides additional LBT values for other listed batch sizes.
rows.check: The prose endpoints and Table I values are correctly recorded but come from separate presentations; do not assume identical experimental conditions without qualification.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9 and AGS
rows.operation_detail: Apply adaptive gradient scaling during large-batch training
rows.note: AGS mitigates the large-batch degradation, but the study says LARS and PoLo observed slightly higher accuracy for ResNet50.
rows.check: The values show mitigation: AGS improves accuracy over LBT by 5.61, 9.03 and 17.44 percentage points. Being below another mitigation method does not make this partial evidence for V5, which allows the penalty to shrink. No matched small-batch baseline establishes complete recovery.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9 and AGS
rows.operation_detail: Apply adaptive gradient scaling during large-batch training
rows.note: Authors state AGS saw the best accuracy across evaluated batches for VGG11.
rows.check: Values are correct. They establish improvement over same-batch LBT, not recovery to small-batch accuracy. AGS accuracy still declines from 84.42 to 81.14% across the listed batches.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with momentum factor 0.9 and AGS
rows.operation_detail: Apply adaptive gradient scaling during large-batch training
rows.note: The flattened Table I layout lists AlexNet LBT values 80.62, 72.80, 62.60 for batches 256, 512, 1024, while the listed AGS values are 84.44, 83.00, 81.20. The paper text says LARS and PoLo observed slightly higher accuracy for AlexNet. The table's condition-to-value mapping for the two large batch entries is not fully clear; baseline values here are not confidently assignable.
rows.check: The table mapping is recoverable: batches are 256, 512 and 1024; LBT accuracies are 80.62, 72.80 and 62.60%; AGS accuracies are 84.44, 83.00 and 81.20%. Remove batch 2048 and the duplicated values. These results show mitigation, without establishing complete small-batch recovery.

rows.check: Values are correct. They establish improvement over same-batch LBT, not complete small-batch recovery; AGS accuracy still declines from 81.56 to 75.70% across the listed batches.

relationships.condition: Unadapted batch-size sweeps for four convolutional image classifiers under the reported epoch schedules
relationships.reason: R1–R4 report declining held-out accuracy as batches grow; prose endpoints include AlexNet 82→37% and MobileNetv3 80→20%.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports declining held-out accuracy with larger batches across four convolutional classifiers, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: AGS adaptation versus vanilla training at matching large batch sizes
relationships.reason: R5–R8 show higher held-out accuracy with AGS at every tabulated batch, supporting V5's recipe-dependent mitigation clause; they do not establish complete recovery.
relationships.display_finding: AGS reportedly improved held-out accuracy over vanilla training at matching large batches, but the comparisons remain unverified and do not establish complete recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
